reason: Tool call #55 can never return: its `timeout 180` already fired and killed the outer python ~15 min ago, but the inner `sp.run(xvfb-run dbus-run-session ..., timeout=170)` leaked the dbus-session tree (pids 2528132-35, reparented to init, 0% CPU) which still holds the stdout pipe write end feeding `tail -30`, so the bash call blocks forever with no CPU. The agent cannot self-diagnose this from a killed tool call and its next probe uses the same pipe-to-tail + sp.run(timeout) pattern, so it walks straight back into the same trap; note also the inner lab run itself hung (never finished in 170s vs 24s in call #53).
message: Your tool call #55 hung permanently and was killed by the supervisor — do NOT re-run it as-is. WHAT HUNG: `timeout 180 env IME_ACQUIRE_LAB=1 python - <<EOF ... 2>&1 | tail -30`. WHY: when your inner `sp.run(["xvfb-run","-a","dbus-run-session",...], timeout=170)` timed out it SIGKILLed only xvfb-run; the dbus-run-session/dbus-daemon/inner-python children survived, were reparented to init, and kept the stdout pipe open, so `tail -30` never saw EOF and the whole bash call sat at 0% CPU forever. `timeout 180` cannot fix this — it only signals the direct python child, and a pipe to tail/head only completes when EVERY fd holder exits. Two more facts: (a) the inner lab run itself hung this time (stuck ~15 min at 0% CPU; it did NOT merely need more than 170s), while the identical lab via call #53 finished in 24s — so compare your stripped inner env before assuming a timeout issue; (b) the supervisor already killed the leaked orphans (Xvfb :99, dbus session, inner python, wl-copy); the preserved run dir /tmp/ime-acquire-lab-jxm0_zh5 was empty. THE SAFE PATTERN from now on: (1) never pipe a GUI-session-spawning run into tail/head — redirect to a bounded log file and read it after the command exits: `timeout 180 env IME_ACQUIRE_LAB=1 .venv/bin/python - >/tmp/ime_dbg.log 2>&1 <<'EOF' ... EOF; echo exit=$?; tail -40 /tmp/ime_dbg.log`. (2) Launch the nested session with subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) and on timeout os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGTERM), then SIGKILL after 5s, so the dbus session dies with it. (3) Before each lab run, clean leftovers: `pkill -f 'ime-acquire-lab|dbus-run-session.*ime-acquire|Xvfb :99'` and remove stale /tmp/ime-acquire-lab-* dirs (this repo's /tmp is a RAM-backed tmpfs — keep scratch bounded).
